The SVP will set and execute the technology vision for Wealth Services, with end-to-end accountability for architecture, engineering, platform delivery, operational resilience, cybersecurity, data, and strategic partner integration across State Street’s Wealth Custody & Clearing business. The role will shape enterprise investment priorities and lead to the modernization and scaling of custody, clearing, advisor, and client platforms through a cloud-native, API-first strategy.

Why This Role is important to us
Wealth Services Technology is building State Street’s next-generation wealth platform, spanning broker-dealer, custody, clearing, advisor, and digital client capabilities. The organization operates at the intersection of business strategy, technology transformation, regulatory accountability, and strategic partnerships.

This role is accountable for establishing the technology direction, governance, operating model, and execution discipline required to deliver secure, resilient, and scalable solutions. The SVP will influence enterprise strategy, advise senior executives, and align technology investment to growth, client, risk, and financial outcomes. The position is critical to expanding the business, protecting the franchise, and delivering differentiated capabilities to institutional and RIA clients.
What you will be responsible for

As a Senior Vice President, you will:
- Set and execute the multi-year Wealth Services technology strategy and target architecture, aligning priorities with business growth, client commitments, enterprise standards, and risk appetite.
- Own the Wealth Services technology portfolio including, but not limited to, the following: investment roadmap, operating plan, and financial performance, including prioritization, funding decisions, benefits realization, vendor spend, and cost optimization.
- Provide executive sponsorship for the design and delivery of a scalable, cloud-native platform supporting account opening, trading, clearing, settlement, custody, portfolio accounting, compliance, and reporting.
- Establish architecture and engineering standards, including API-first, event-driven, data, cybersecurity, and resilience patterns that enable secure integration and real-time processing.
- Lead the technology strategy and executive governance for third-party clearing and custody relationships with clear accountability for delivery, service levels, controls, concentration risk, and commercial outcomes.

This pivotal role sits at the intersection of enterprise risk architecture and cutting-edge Generative AI. Are you interested in growing your career in Cyber Security?

Whether you are an application developer or researcher looking to make the switch into the challenging, yet rewarding, world of information security, or you are an elite white-hat hacker, Citi is the place for you. Our team of world class, talented individuals, who are passionate about security, put their skills to the test every day on a global scale. At Citi, you will be exposed to all sorts of technologies on an enterprise-scale, so hunger for knowledge and research is greatly appreciated and rewarded.

Technology is constantly evolving, and Citi is evolving with it by adopting the latest application frameworks, migrating to cloud-based technologies, and implementing Artificial Intelligence in numerous workflows across the enterprise. Citi’s application penetration testing team is at the forefront of testing and securing each of these solutions and you can make an impact on the next technology to be released.

This team specializes in conducting various types of penetration testing engagements (full end-to-end white-box and/or grey-box testing) against a variety of Citi owned or 3rd party SaaS applications (Web, Mobile, Thick Client, and APIs) leveraging a wide array of technologies from Artificial Intelligence, to Digital Assets, Blockchain, and more traditional application development frameworks. The primary goal would be to secure Citi, its customers, and clients by manually identifying, researching, validating, and exploiting application security weaknesses and misconfigurations.

Core responsibilities include:

-
- Plan, scope, and execute comprehensive penetration tests against blockchain networks, smart contracts, decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols, and digital asset custody systems.
- Perform manual and automated source code reviews of smart contracts written in Solidity, Rust, Go, or Vyper to identify logic flaws, reentrancy, front-running, flash loan vulnerabilities, and integer overflows.
- Act as a subject matter expert in offensive information security performing dynamic and manual security assessments on web technologies such as APIs, JavaScript Frameworks, Artificial Intelligence, and Distributed Ledger Technologies.
- Drive remediation by outlining a defense-in-depth approach to business stakeholders and providing strategic solutions to developers on effective preventive and detective security controls.
- Have strong technical writing and presentation skills to report and articulate the vulnerability assessment results to any audience.
- Contribute to the review of internal processes and activities and assist in identifying potential opportunities for improvement and automation.
- Conduct research into emerging attack vectors, zero-day exploits, and novel vulnerabilities unique to Web3 and digital asset ecosystems
- Must have or be willing to obtain Industry-accredited security certifications such as: BSCP, GWAPT, GPEN, OSCP, OSWE, CISSP, or other related certifi

**Organization:** National Nonprofit Organization  
**Reports To:** Chief Executive Officer  
**Department:** Technology  
**Work Location:** Remote  
**Employment Status:** Regular, Full-Time, Exempt  
**Position Level:** Executive / Senior Leadership  
**Salary Range:** $225,000–$250,000 annually

**ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION**

We are a national nonprofit organization committed to advancing our mission through innovative programs, strategic partnerships, and technology-enabled services. We work with diverse stakeholders across the country to deliver programs, strengthen operations, and achieve meaningful outcomes.

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Chief Technology Officer to lead our technology function, strengthen operational performance, and guide the continued evolution of our technology infrastructure and digital platforms.

This is an opportunity to join our executive leadership team and play a critical role in shaping our technology strategy, strengthening our systems and capabilities, and ensuring technology supports our organizational mission and long-term priorities.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) serves as our senior technology executive and technical authority, with overall accountability for enterprise technology strategy, engineering, infrastructure, cybersecurity, data governance, and technology delivery.

This is a hands-on executive leadership role requiring a combination of deep technical expertise, strategic thinking, business acumen, and operational leadership. The CTO directly supervises the technology team, provides technical direction, oversees production changes, and ensures the reliability, security, and performance of our critical systems.

The position combines responsibilities often distributed across an engineering manager, vice president of engineering, and chief technology officer. The successful candidate must be equally comfortable making complex technical decisions, leading a multidisciplinary team, developing long-term technology strategies, and advising executive leadership on investments, operational risks, and organizational priorities.

The CTO leads a team of employees and contractors responsible for enterprise applications, digital platforms, data and reporting systems, cloud infrastructure, and internal IT operations. The role carries direct accountability for the availability, performance, security, and continued modernization of business-critical systems.

**POSITION DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Executive Leadership and Accountability:** Serve as a member of the executive leadership team, advising the CEO and senior leaders on technology strategy, investments, risks, and opportunities. Translate complex technical matters into business implications and contribute to organizational strategy, resource planning, and executive and board discussions.
* **Team Leadership and Supervision:** Directly supervise engineering, analysis, and IT staff

As a Senior AI Engineer specializing in Python and agentic systems, you will architect the generative and agentic AI solutions that power Citi's Controls Technology platform, working at the frontier of context engineering, retrieval systems, and multi-agent orchestration. You will design production-grade AI systems that are grounded, reliable, and built to operate at enterprise scale, partnering with AI architects, engineering leads, and business stakeholders across one of the world's most complex financial institutions. Your work will strengthen automation and operational efficiency across teams, products, and the millions of clients and communities Citi serves every day.

Responsibilities:
- Design and build generative and agentic AI solutions in Python that solve real business problems across Citi's Controls Technology platform.
- Architect context engineering strategies, including context layering, chaining, compression, and memory management, to keep production AI systems reliable and token-efficient.
- Build and optimize Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems using hybrid search, multi-vector retrieval, and re-ranking pipelines.
- Design knowledge graphs and Graph RAG architectures that enable multi-hop reasoning and traceable, grounded responses for high-value business domains.

We’ve pioneered a memory-centric architecture that brings compute directly into memory, making AI faster, more energy efficient, and accessible on a global scale.  - Hire and lead the platform software team, owning technical direction, milestones, quality, and on-call, and convert open architecture documents into owned, dated deliverables.

Navan is seeking a strategic, builder-minded Head of Applied AI Engineering to turn cutting-edge AI capabilities into measurable business impact across our organization. Sitting at the intersection of engineering, product, and business operations, you will own Navan’s internal applied AI strategy—identifying high-leverage operational opportunities, architecting our internal AI ecosystem, and accelerating how every department builds and deploys AI solutions.
In this role, you will treat our internal AI platforms and agentic frameworks as internal products, partner with business leaders to move high-ROI use cases from prototype to production, and lead a cross-functional network of AI Champions that embeds an AI-first operating model across the company.

What You'll Do
- Own Applied AI Strategy & Execution: Define and execute Navan’s internal applied AI roadmap—partnering with department heads to identify, prioritize, and ship high-ROI automation and agentic workflows tied to productivity, margin, and speed.

- Bridge Prototypes to Production: Partner closely with business units and core engineering/IT teams to take high-value proof-of-concept (POC) builds and harden them into secure, reliable, production-grade internal solutions.
- Scale an AI Champion Network & Builder Culture: Build, mentor, and energize a cross-departmental community of AI Champions—equipping employees with the frameworks, reusable templates, and technical guidance needed to build autonomous workflows within their own functions.
- Establish Applied Governance & Evaluation: Partner with Security, Legal, and Data teams to implement practical guardrails, data privacy standards, and evaluation frameworks so teams can innovate rapidly without compromising trust or compliance.

What We're Looking For:
- Enablement & Change Leadership: Demonstrated success designing and leading practical technical enablement, building active builder communities, and translating complex AI capabilities into clear, actionable playbooks for non-technical teams.
- Deep Applied AI Fluency: Strong hands-on command of the modern applied AI landscape—including frontier LLMs, agentic workflows, RAG architectures, API integrations, and AI automation platforms—with an instinct for matching the right tool to the right business problem.
- Builder & Prototyping Track Record: Proven ability to rapidly architect, test, and validate functional AI solutions and agents, with experience transitioning successful pilots into durable operational workflows.
- Internal Product & Platform Mindset: Experience managing internal tools, developer platforms, or enablement ecosystems as products—using user feedback, telemetry, and adoption metrics to drive continuous iteration.

**The Company**

colliga is building deterministic governance for probabilistic AI systems (large language models to start). It checks what a probabilistic model produces against the rules an enterprise has set, determines admissibility, and keeps a versioned, replayable record of every decision. It works mid-stream, and only returns responses that are fully compliant, thus replacing traditional guardrails.

**The problem**

Businesses deploying AI are discovering that a model usually behaves as trained with current governance techniques, but not always. "Usually" is not good enough for high-stakes use-cases, and therefore not something a regulator, auditor or buyer's legal or security teams will sign off on. As a result, AI is failing to reach its full potential for critical tasks. A governed, logged, deterministic gate can turn "usually" into "always, provably, and with evidence" for many of these systems.

We hold a family of 14 filed patents, have a working prototype and a proof of concept, and are ready to build the first production product.

The Chief Technology Officer is the technical owner of that thesis: what is built, what works, what the evidence supports, and what the company can honestly promise customers and investors. You will be the single technical voice who sets direction, arbitrates between competing designs, and leads the engineers who build it.

You lead the engineering team and own the code and infrastructure, with authority over technical direction, hiring, architecture, security posture and engineering process. ABOUT MATTER HEALTH

Matter Health delivers primary and preventive healthcare directly to older adults living in affordable housing communities. Our mission is simple: to improve healthcare access by meeting patients where they are and building trusted relationships within the communities we serve.

As we rapidly expand, we are seeking mission-driven professionals who thrive in fast-paced, people-centered environments.

We Lead with Love in Everything We Do.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Matter Health is seeking an experienced Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) to lead and continuously strengthen our enterprise information security program.

Our value-based care model depends on the trust of our patients, providers, and payer partners. Protecting sensitive health information across our distributed, field-based care delivery model is essential to maintaining that trust.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, the CISO will be responsible for developing and executing Matter Health's information security strategy, establishing security policies and governance frameworks, overseeing cybersecurity operations, and ensuring compliance with applicable healthcare security regulations.

This is a high-visibility, hands-on executive leadership opportunity for someone who enjoys building and scaling security programs within a growing healthcare organization. The CISO will work closely with Technology, Clinical Operations, Compliance, and executive leadership to strengthen organizational security while supporting continued growth.

The position will initially oversee a cybersecurity analyst and work alongside an external contractor supporting Matter Health's HITRUST certification efforts.

The ideal candidate brings deep healthcare cybersecurity expertise, strong executive leadership capabilities, and the ability to balance enterprise-level security standards with the flexibility and adaptability required in a growth-stage environment.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Information Security Strategy & Leadership

 - Develop, implement, and continuously evolve Matter Health's enterprise information security strategy, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, clinical operations, and regulatory requirements.

 - Establish and maintain security policies, standards, and procedures covering data protection, access controls, acceptable use, and third-party risk management.

 - Build and mature security governance frameworks, including NIST CSF and HITRUST CSF, appropriate for an organization handling protected health information (PHI).

 - Lead security budget planning, vendor selection, and technology investments while balancing security needs with organizational priorities.

 - Manage and develop internal cybersecurity resources while collaborating with external security partners and consultants.

 - Provide regular security updates, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership, including occasional presentations to the Board of Directors.

Centage is building the AI Finance Department: a managed-service team that walks into the CFO's office at a $50M to $500M company, maps where finance time goes, ranks those hours by dollar value, and ships the first production workflow within 90 days.  
  
We start from a foundation most AI services firms don't have: more than 500 finance teams already run their close, budgets, forecasts, cash, consolidation, and board reporting on our FP&A platform. Our promise to every customer is that we build agents that automate their finance workflows, governed so a controller can trace every number, secure enough for their auditor, and built to scale across their entities.  
  
The internal measure we care about most is time to value.

You own the team that delivers the AI Finance Department to every customer we sign, and you report to the CEO. This is a player-coach role: you set the standard, hire the team, and still ship the hardest deployment yourself when it matters.

About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

About the role
Cloudflare is hiring a Head of Zero Day Engineering to build and lead the team that turns newly discovered vulnerabilities into verified protection—for Cloudflare and its customers.
High-priority vulnerabilities rarely fit within one team’s boundaries. A fix may require kernel expertise, changes across software dependencies and trust stores, fleet-wide deployment, customer-facing WAF protections, and investigation of prior exploitation. You will bring those efforts together, with clear ownership from initial disclosure through verified remediation.
This is a hands-on engineering leadership role. You will recruit the team, establish its operating model, and build the tooling that makes response faster and more reliable. You will combine experienced human judgment with carefully evaluated AI-assisted workflows—not automate away accountability.
What you’ll do
Build and lead the team
- Establish Zero Day Engineering’s charter, priorities, operating model, and partnerships across Cloudflare.
- Recruit, develop, and lead engineers spanning vulnerability response, exposure analysis, mitigation, patching, artifact provenance, release coordination, and automation.
- Build a sustainable incident-command rotation, clear escalation paths, and effective handoffs across teams and time zones.
- Create a culture of technical depth, calm execution, blameless learning, and shared accountability.
Own vulnerability response end to end

The National Cancer Institute (NCI) is seeking an innovative leader to serve as the Director, Center for Biomedical Informatics and Information Technology (CBIIT), located in the Office of the Director (OD), National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health (NIH). The Director, CBIIT is classified under the Title 42 hiring mechanism and is equivalent to an extramural Program Division Director position. The position reports to the NCI Deputy Director for Data Science and Strategy. The Director, CBIIT leads the federal government components in the cancer research IT and informatics enterprise. In this capacity, the CBIIT Director delivers executive and managerial leadership and oversight for NCI-wide cybersecurity, use of IT, alignment with federal IT policies and requirements. The position also provides data science and informatics vision to NCI data science, informatics, and computational investments, including advancing the use of artificial intelligence across the research and operational spectrum. The Director, CBIIT oversees the implementation of the NCI cancer data ecosystem, the function of the NCI CIO, and coordinates data science and research data access for NCI at a national level.
  
Duties
  
  
The Director, CBIIT, is responsible for oversight of critical NCI information systems including systems that support clinical trials data, cancer data standards, multimodal cancer research data, and NCI grants information and other key business systems. The position manages a budget of approximately $240 million dollars, overseeing a federal workforce of approximately 90 people and more than 600 contractors engaged in providing IT, biomedical research informatics and software infrastructure and services to NCI. The CBIIT Director also participates in the scientific leadership of NCI and in NCI research initiatives and represents NCI with relevant national and international research communities. The CBIIT Director will also build strong working relationships that foster a strong, vibrant cohesive team across NCI.

At Valar Atomics, we're redefining what's possible in energy. Our mission is to make clean, high-temperature nuclear power scalable—unlocking abundant energy for industry, hydrogen, and next-generation manufacturing. We are a team of builders, engineers, and operators who believe nuclear energy should be fast to deploy, factory-made, and built for the real world. Our first pilot plant in Orangeville, Utah will demonstrate how advanced nuclear systems and fuel fabrication can power the future. Joining Valar Atomics means becoming part of a company where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level.

The Team

The Numenor team is building Valar’s next reactor, the flagship program that will define how we deliver nuclear power at scale. This dedicated team owns the entire plant, from the reactor core and helium systems to cooling, plant modules, and the Citadel, uniting mechanical, systems, safety, IC&E, quality, and supply chain under one mission. The work starts with bringing the first unit to life and ends with a production line that delivers reactors faster with every build. What this team builds will power the critical infrastructure of the future.

Valar Atomics seeks a Director, Systems Engineering for the reactor program. This role will build and lead the systems engineering organization for the reactor program. The scope covers the systems engineering process, the product breakdown structure (PBS), and the structure and technical accuracy of the reactor design basis. The role will lead systems integration and engineering from the first unit through scaled production, delivering reactors at an increasing rate.

The role demands someone who can develop, implement, and maintain a systems engineering architecture and high-value tools that enable Valar to produce and license Numenor series reactors at scale. Success in this role means producing and maintaining a tight design basis that scales, while always keeping a clear design thread for the required traceability.

At Compass, our mission is to help everyone find their place in the world. Founded in 2012, we're revolutionizing the real estate industry with our end-to-end platform that empowers residential real estate agents to deliver exceptional service to seller and buyer clients.

**About the Role:**

The Director of the Security Operations Center owns detection, response, and threat hunting across our production, corporate, and cloud environments. This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will set the direction of the SOC in line with the CISO's security strategy and run a team of senior technical professionals day to day. When an incident calls for it, you will step in personally and lead the investigation and response. You report directly to the CISO and act as their operational partner, so the CISO always has an accurate picture of threats, exposure, and our ability to respond.

**What you will do:**

* Turn the CISO's security strategy into a SOC roadmap, prioritize where detection and response investment goes, and show measurable progress against it.
* Own the end-to-end detection and response lifecycle, from telemetry collection through detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and corrective action.
* Act as incident commander for the highest-severity events. Get hands-on in the investigation, analyze logs, endpoint, network, identity, and cloud telemetry yourself, and make containment decisions under pressure.
* Build, lead, and develop a team of incident response, detection, and threat hunting engineers. Set a high technical bar, coach people through hard investigations, and hold the team accountable for quality and follow-through.
* Hold your ground on technical and risk decisions with engineering, product, IT, and executive stakeholders. Push back with evidence when a decision increases exposure, and escalate clearly when needed.
* Design and evolve the SOC architecture, including SIEM, SOAR, EDR, identity, and cloud detection tooling. Decide what to build, what to buy, and what to retire.
* Drive an automation-first operating model that cuts manual triage, shortens time to detect and contain, and lets the team scale without adding headcount in step with the environment.
* Establish full telemetry coverage across the Compass platform, including acquired environments, so that every critical asset produces attributable, correlated events.
* Lead a threat-informed defense program. Use adversary behavior, threat intelligence, and hunting results to drive detection engineering and active defense capabilities.
* Own the incident response plan, severity definitions, escalation paths, and on-call model. Run realistic tabletop and live-fire exercises that include technical teams and executives.
* Run blameless post-incident reviews and make sure corrective actions have an identified owner, a deadline, and verified completion.
* Define and report the operational metrics that matter, such as coverage, detection fidelity, dwell time,

We are Digital Science and we are advancing the research ecosystem.

In creating the next generation of tools and working in partnership with the community we tackle some of the biggest challenges to research. Your new role

DS has grown through acquisition, and its products, data and engineering practices have grown up separately. This role leads the move from that fragmented portfolio to one platform: a single data platform and shared services that every DS product builds on, run by engineering teams working to a consistent operating model.

The VP owns engineering best practice across the group, defines and rolls out a single Target Operating Model (TOM) for engineering, and leads the transformation of today's operating model onto it. The role also owns the foundational layers of the platform (data platform, identity and access, logging, licensing and other shared services) and is accountable for their adoption by product and engineering teams.

The core challenge is to make the whole greater than the sum of its parts. Products should share data, services and standards, while current customer commitments and revenue-critical data releases stay dependable through the transition. Success means a trusted, reusable and commercially valuable data foundation, less duplicated capability, and faster, more consistent delivery across DS.

The VP also works with the Chief AI Officer to deliver the AI plan, and manages the transition of DS engineering to an AI-first software development lifecycle (SDLC).

Engineering strategy and operating model

• Agree an incremental platform roadmap with product leadership, with visible dependencies, early wins and clear progress measures.
• Lead adoption as well as build: agree integration paths with product teams, reduce duplicated capability and retire legacy components.
• Lead the rollout of an AI-first operating model across engineering, setting standards for AI-enabled development practices.

Unified data platform

• Deliver one data platform that underpins all DS applications and brings together data sources from across the group.

• Establish enrichment as a reusable platform capability, with clear ownership and a route to modernise long-standing algorithms and processes.

This is a greenfield role. You'll build a product management practice, shape an entirely new category at AWS, and establish the engagement model that delivers delightful outcomes enabling customers to transform themselves.

**The Role**

As the Director of Product Management — Forward Deployed Engineering will lead product management for FDE, building and leading the PM team that owns the end-to-end product lifecycle from customer engagement through production delivery through optimization and self-sufficiency. Your product managers embed directly inside enterprise customers — defining outcomes, writing specs, working hand-in-hand with engineering to ship production systems — and every engagement feeds back into AWS services and an underlying platform that makes the next one faster.

This is not a traditional AWS Product Management role. FDE product managers are field-facing: they live inside delivery, sit with customers, and turn engagement learnings into compounding platform value. You are the "CEO of the customer problem" — responsible for the *why* and *what*, while engineering owns the *how*.

Key job responsibilities
### Product Leadership

You own the customer outcomes. Your teams operate inside customer environments under real constraints and ambitious timelines — regulated data, brownfield infrastructure, multi-stakeholder governance. You lead the customer engagement strategy from the product side: define what a great pod PM does, allocate PM talent across engagements, ensure pods are solving the right problems, and hold executive customer relationships at the CIO/CTO level built on trust earned through delivered outcomes.

### Product & Platform Influence

You see what breaks  across deployments and turn that into product direction. You influence AWS service roadmap from a position of earned authority because you've lived the deployment pain firsthand, and identify when custom pod work should graduate into platform primitives or native service capabilities.

You shape the FDE engagement model: how we scope, what we deliver, what we price, what we leave behind.

### Industry Practice & Productization

You build the domain expertise that compounds. Your teams develop industry-specific accelerators, reference architectures, and blueprints that generate pipeline for the next customer in your vertical. You define the use cases that feed qualification, pricing, and pod composition. You measure what matters: asset reuse rate, time-to-value, engagement velocity

### Go-to-Market Partnership

You partner with sales, specialists, and marketing to define pricing, packaging, and positioning. You own the commercial model for FDE engagements — how we price outcomes, what the customer buys, and how we demonstrate ROI. You build pipeline through customer stories, reference architectures

Small businesses represent 99.9% of all companies, yet they're still forced to choose between clunky, outdated enterprise phone systems or their personal phones. This multi-billion dollar market has been overlooked for decades, left to cobble together solutions that slow them down instead of helping them grow.

 

Quo is changing that. We bring calls, texts, and customer information together into one easy-to-use, AI-powered platform. We're not just building a phone system. We're setting a new standard for how businesses connect with their customers.

 

Driven by our values, we move fast, build with determination, and obsess over delivering value to the businesses that have been underserved for far too long.

roles.description:
Build AI That Could Help Transform the Future of Medicine

Frontier AI is changing what’s possible in science, and few places let you apply it to a problem as consequential as human health. Pfizer is one of them. We have decades of world-class biology and chemistry, rich biomedical data and the global reach to get medicines to patients. We are pairing them with the newest advances in AI and we are doing it along with the world’s leaders in building medicine.

At Pfizer, we believe the next generation of scientific breakthroughs will be powered by advances in artificial intelligence. From foundation models and multimodal learning to biological reasoning and agentic systems, AI has the potential to fundamentally change how we discover, develop, and deliver medicines to patients.  You will help create the scientific foundations behind that future at Pfizer.

We are not looking for one clever model for one clever problem or applying existing models to a single problem. You will develop, extend, and rigorously evaluate advanced AI methods that generate new scientific insights, accelerate experimentation, and enable better decision-making across the drug discovery and development lifecycle. We are building AI that compounds. A method, benchmark or model that works in one disease area should become a foundation that can impact across oncology, immunology/inflammation, internal medicine, vaccines and beyond. You’ll design for that!

Working alongside world-class AI researchers, computational biologists, engineers, and domain experts, you'll tackle some of the most challenging and meaningful problems in healthcare while building technology that has the potential to impact millions of patients worldwide.

Why This Role Is Different
Own Meaningful Scientific Challenges: You will own defined model components, benchmarks, evaluation frameworks, and research workflows that directly influence how AI is applied across Pfizer's R&D organization. You'll build the models, and you'll also decide whether they create real scientific value and whether that value holds up in new contexts.

Where you will push the frontier:  You'll contribute to cutting-edge research across areas such as:

-
- Foundation models and representation learning.
- Multimodal learning across molecular, imaging, clinical and omics data
- Agentic AI and scientific reasoning systems
- Biological Sequence & Structure Modeling
- Graph learning and knowledge graphs
- Clinical & Real-World Data Modeling
- Uncertainty-Aware AI, causal ML and Interpretability

Create Impact Beyond Research Papers
Publishing matters, but the goal is bigger. Your work will help scientists understand disease biology, prioritize experiments, and evaluate therapeutic opportunities across the portfolio. It will speed up medicines for the people waiting on them.

Work at the frontier, with the people who can ship it to patients.

Summary
  
Fairbanks Morse Defense builds and supports the engines, power systems, and mechanical systems that keep Navy and Coast Guard ships underway. Our technology organization develops the next generation of those products, modernizes the equipment already in the fleet, and guides where FMD invests across its product lines.
  
We are hiring a Director of Technology to lead that organization. You will own three things: technology development and internal R&D investment, the retrofit and upgrade business that modernizes in-service engines and systems, and product portfolio management across FMD. You will set the technology roadmap, lead the engineering and product teams that deliver it, and report to the Sr. Vice President of Strategic Projects.
  
This role is remote, leading a team out of Beloit Wisconsin, with approximately 35% travel to FMD facilities, customer sites, shipyards, and test sites.
  
Why This Role
  

* The full technology lifecycle. You own products from early R&D through military qualification, fielding, and in-service upgrade.
* A fleet that needs modernizing. FMD engines and systems are installed across the Navy, Coast Guard, and Military Sealift Command fleets. Your retrofit and upgrade programs extend their service life, improve readiness, and solve obsolescence.
* A portfolio view across FMD. You see every product line in the company and shape where FMD invests, and sustains.
* Customer and executive access. You work directly with Navy technical authorities, program offices, and research sponsors, and with FMD’s executive team and business leaders.
* A mission that matters. Your products help keep global naval and coast guard vessels powered, ready, and supported.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities
  

* Technology Strategy & Development
* Define and maintain FMD’s technology roadmap for power, propulsion, controls, and digital sustainment products, aligned to Global Navy’s, Coast Guard’s, and other customers priorities.
* Own the internal R&D (IRAD) portfolio: select projects, set gates and exit criteria, allocate budget, and stop work that is not earning continued investment.
* Lead development programs from concept through prototype, test, military qualification (shock, vibration, and electromagnetic interference), and transition to production.
* Pursue and execute government-funded development with sponsors such as NSWCPD, ONR, NAVSEA, and DIU, including white papers, proposals, and prototype agreements under Other Transaction Authority.
* Build and manage relationships with engine licensors, technology partners, universities, and government test sites.
* Retrofits & Upgrades
* Own the retrofit and upgrade product line for in-service engines and systems, including fuel system upgrades (common rail and electronic fuel injection), controls modernization, and obsolescence solutions.

**Summary**
-----------

This position is located in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Management Directorate, Office of the Chief Information Office (OCIO). The DHS OCIO is responsible for all matters relating to information and DHS information environment including customer experience, network operations, information systems, information assurance, defensive cybersecurity, and communications.

Learn more about this agency

  

**This job is open to**
-----------------------

### **The public**

U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.

### **Federal employees - Competitive service**

Current federal employees whose agencies follow the U.S. Office of Personnel Management's hiring rules and pay scales.

### **Federal employees - Excepted service**

Current federal employees whose agencies have their own hiring rules, pay scales and evaluation criteria.

### **Senior executives**

Individuals looking for an executive-level job and who meet the five Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs).

### **Clarification from the agency**

All groups of qualified individuals - ALL US CITIZENS

  

**Duties**
----------

The Executive Director, Mission Delivery Directorate (XD, MDD) serves as the Department's senior executive responsible for technology product delivery, software engineering, enterprise architecture, data strategy, digital services, customer experience, and platform modernization. The Executive Director is responsible for transforming how technology capabilities are designed, developed, delivered, and continuously improved across DHS. XD MDD plays a central role in advancing the Department's technology modernization strategy by establishing enterprise platforms, enabling data-driven decision making, accelerating software delivery, improving customer experiences, and ensuring technology investments produce measurable mission outcomes.
  
  
Specific responsibilities include:

* Serves as the principal advisor on DHS enterprise technology strategy, digital transformation, data management, and product delivery. In partnership with the CIO and DCIO, the XD MDD leads Department mission delivery through the effective use of information resources and technology.
* Leads the DHS Mission Delivery Directorate and provides executive oversight for enterprise software development, product management, digital services, data strategy, enterprise architecture, and technology innovation.

We are building the future of patient engagement for life sciences companies. Our software is leveraged by biopharma companies to support patients in their complex journey from diagnosis to initiating and remaining on therapy to achieve optimal health outcomes.

**Come Build with Us**
----------------------

We're an NYC-based team that believes culture, craft, and customer obsession go hand in hand. We show up for each other the same way we show up for the people we serve. We're an office-first company that values in-person collaboration 4 days per week because we believe the best work happens when you can collaborate and brainstorm together in the same room. If that sounds like your kind of place, we think you'll love it here.

**The Opportunity**
-------------------

Courier Health is at an inflection point. We exist to get patients faster, better access to life-saving therapies. Patients trust us with their health information, and the pharma companies we serve trust us to protect it. That trust is what lets the mission scale. This role owns that.

As Director of Security, you will report to the CTO and set direction for security across three surfaces: the Courier platform and the AI agents running on it, how our engineers build that platform, and how we run the company. IT Operations reports through you, and you will set the direction for security architecture across Courier.

This is a build job. We are putting AI agents into patient workflows that touch PHI, and the playbook for securing that is still being written. You will write it. And you will use agents to run a security program that covers far more ground than its headcount suggests.

**What You'll Build**
---------------------

**A platform that earns a pharma security team's trust.** You will set the direction for security architecture of the Courier platform and our AI agents, threat-modeling agent workflows for prompt injection, tool and permission boundaries, and data leakage before they ship. Nuclear fusion represents the ultimate clean energy solution. We are reviving a promising 1980s magnetic confinement reactor architecture, with a unique plasma stabilization mechanism. Modern technology resolves the historical power limitations of the concept, enabling stable, steady-state confinement and paving the way for scalable fusion power.

We’re looking for a technical co-founder to the venture. This role presents an extraordinary opportunity to translate core scientific objectives into robust, operable, and scalable fusion hardware, while steering a high-impact commercial venture onto the global stage. The aim is to spin the company out of DSV over the coming months.

As Chief Technology Officer, you will lead the technology and engineering roadmap, own the overall system architecture and subsystem integration. You will lead the translation of scientific requirements into safe, operable and progressively more capable fusion systems, from experimental machines toward a neutron source and eventual power plant.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Lead the technology and engineering roadmap.
* Own the architecture and integration of the experimental platform and supporting systems.
* Translate scientific objectives into engineering requirements, specifications and test plans.
* Lead the design, construction, commissioning and operation of experimental hardware.
* Direct the progression from research platform to neutron-source and reactor systems.
* Lead integrated reactor engineering and design optimization within the scientific envelope defined by the CSO.

**Ownership & Accountability:**

* Own the system architecture, engineering integrity and demonstrated performance of the company’s integrated technology systems.
* Define engineering requirements, interfaces, operating envelopes and acceptance criteria.
* Own integration across relevant subsystems, including magnets, heating, vacuum, power, thermal management, structures, diagnostics, controls and data acquisition.
* Lead engineering trade-offs across performance, safety, reliability, cost, schedule, maintainability and scalability.
* Own design reviews, configuration management, engineering change control and technical decision records.
* Direct procurement, supplier selection, fabrication, assembly, installation and commissioning.
* Establish procedures for commissioning, operation, maintenance, troubleshooting and system modification.
* Own operational readiness, machine protection, engineering safety and facility reliability.
* Establish a rigorous test, failure-investigation and corrective-action culture that converts technical setbacks into verified design improvements.
* Build and lead a lean engineering capability spanning internal contributors, contractors, suppliers and partners, while retaining system-level accountability.
* Jointly with the CSO, provide technical sign-off on experimental configurations, major development milestones and decisions at the science/e

Wiley is in the midst of a critical technology transformation period, consolidating enterprise technology under unified leadership to accelerate AI adoption, reduce complexity, and deliver seamless digital experiences across the organization. As Senior Leader, Enterprise Infrastructure & Cloud, you will be a cornerstone of that transformation.

This role owns the foundational technology layer that everything else runs on: cloud infrastructure, AI Infrastructure, FinOps, DevOps and delivery engineering capabilities. You will work at the intersection of engineering excellence and business impact—modernizing the platforms that underpin Wiley's research, learning, AI DA and enterprise systems while embedding the automation, reliability, and agility that the enterprise needs to move faster.

Reporting directly to the VP of Infrastructure Services, you will lead globally distributed teams, manage strategic managed service relationships, and play an active role in the broader Enterprise Technology leadership team as Wiley continues to evolve its operating model.

This role incorporates Service Delivery Manager responsibilities related to a managed service agreement — technical ownership, architectural assurance, and domain governance — within the IMS service tower. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

As AI designs more of biology, the bottleneck moves to experiments: running them fast, at scale and with data people can trust. You find the partners where Adaptyv can become core infrastructure. You shape the terms, and you run the deal: scientific scope, pricing, legal, and the internal plan to deliver it. You also design new partnership models and the deals that do not fit a standard quote.

DawnSecurity is building a next-generation cybersecurity platform. At its core is a hard applied-research problem, and this role owns it: leading our Data Science and Data Engineering team, directing algorithm research, building the models behind the platform, and driving the company's intellectual property.

### **What makes this role different**

This is not a "train a classifier on labeled data" role. The core challenges are:

* Learning without labels. The events that matter most are too rare to train on. Models must be built from structure, statistics, and synthetically generated signal rather than labeled examples.
* Probabilistic modeling over graphs. The problem domain is inherently relational — entities, hierarchies, and connections — and the models must reason over that structure, not just over flat feature vectors.
* Adversarially robust learning. An adversary can influence the data our models learn from. Robustness to manipulation and governed model updates are first-class design constraints.
* Explainability as a requirement. Every score must decompose into a sentence a domain expert can act on. Opaque models that outperform explainable ones by a margin still lose here.
* LLMs as components, not oracles. We use LLMs inside pipelines with statistical quality gates and human-in-the-loop escalation — knowing when not to trust model output is the skill.

### **Core Responsibilities**

### **Research & Modeling Leadership**

* Own the research agenda: from hypothesis through prototype, empirical validation, shadow-mode deployment, and production.
* Design probabilistic and statistical models for sparse, high-cardinality event data — scoring, smoothing, calibration, drift detection.
* Lead graph-based modeling: entity resolution across heterogeneous sources, inference over large graphs, relationship discovery with tiered confidence.
* Combine statistical models with rule- and constraint-based reasoning where the two must agree.
* Define the evaluation discipline: synthetic data, shadow-mode comparisons, calibration audits, and precision targets tied to user trust.

### **IP Creation & Protection**

* Drive patentable inventions from the research roadmap: identify novel mechanisms, validate them empirically, and work with patent counsel on claims.
* Distinguish what to file, what to publish, and what to keep as trade secret — and sequence research disclosures accordingly.

### **Engineering & Operational Excellence**

* Architect the sandbox-to-production path: streaming and batch pipelines, feature stores, model serving with low-latency inference at high event throughput.
* Establish MLOps: versioning of code, data, and models; automated validation; monitoring that triggers governed retraining.
* Balance startup velocity against platform sustainability; keep compute costs proportionate to value.

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Manufacturing Engineering Team is seeking a Director, Industrial Engineering to lead IE strategy and execution for the Air Defense & Strike (AD&S) division. The Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware — including static equipment, moving ground equipment, sensors, undersea, and flight vehicles — and scaling these products across our production footprint, including our new 5M sq ft manufacturing facility, Arsenal-1.

Industrial Engineering at Anduril operates in a matrix with a Center of Excellence (COE) and embedded IEs directly into the divisions they support. Every embedded IE takes day-to-day direction and priorities from their business line, while the central IE organization provides the methodology, standards, tools, mentorship, career development, surge coverage, and cross-divisional visibility that make each individual IE more effective than they could be on their own. The Director, IE — AD&S is the senior IE leader dedicated to one of Anduril’s highest-growth, most operationally complex divisions — owning the IE strategy, team, and results for AD&S and operating as a peer member of the division’s production leadership team.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Director, Industrial Engineering — AD&S, you will own the industrial engineering function for the Air Defense & Strike division end-to-end. You will build, lead, and develop the IE team embedded in AD&S — hiring the right people, designing the team structure, and setting the IE agenda in lockstep with the division’s production strategy and ramp trajectory and COE standards and enterprise vision / system. By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.
Why join the Harvard Radcliffe Institute?
The Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University, known colloquially as Harvard Radcliffe Institute, is one of the world’s leading centers for interdisciplinary exploration. We bring together students, scholars, artists, and practitioners to pursue curiosity-driven research, expand human understanding, and grapple with questions that demand insight from across disciplines.
The Fellowship Program annually supports the work of 50 leading artists and scholars. Academic Ventures fosters collaborative research projects and sponsors lectures and conferences that engage scholars with the public. The Schlesinger Library documents the lives of American women of the past and present for the future, furthering the Institute's commitment to women, gender, and society. The Emerging Leaders Program is a youth leadership development program partnering local high school sophomores with Harvard undergraduates in a mentoring relationship.
The Institute’s work is shaped by its history as the former Radcliffe College—a school founded to ensure that the standard of education embodied in Harvard was accessible to women, who were then excluded from the University. But the legacy of Radcliffe College is not simply coeducation at Harvard; it is the recognition that universities will always be greater when they draw wisdom and talent from the widest possible pool.
Take a look at this video to get different staff perspectives on working at Harvard Radcliffe Institute !

**A Day in the Life:**

The Director of IT Service Management leads the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of Hertz’s global IT service management practices. This role turns technology and business priorities into reliable, measurable service operations, supporting a consistent experience for employees and business partners across the company.

Working with Technology and business leaders, the Director oversees key service management processes and the systems that support them, including ServiceNow. The role partners closely with infrastructure, end-user services, application, cybersecurity, and operations teams to improve service quality, system stability, resiliency, and compliance. It also manages team performance, budgets, and vendor relationships within the scope of responsibility, using operational data and service metrics to guide decisions and improvements.

**What You’ll Do:**

* Lead, develop, and motivate the IT Service Management team, setting clear goals and supporting employee growth and technical capability.
* Translate business and Technology priorities into service management plans, operational goals, and measurable outcomes.
* Develop and maintain an innovative IT Service Management roadmap that prioritizes automation and modernizes processes, tools, and service delivery in support of Hertz’s business and Technology goals.
* Lead and continuously improve service management processes, including Incident, Request, Problem, Change, Service Level, Event, Service Catalog, and Configuration Management (CMDB).
* Use KPIs, service data, and customer feedback to identify performance gaps, manage backlogs, and prioritize process and system improvements.
* Oversee the ServiceNow platform roadmap and backlog, partnering with stakeholders on enhancements, automation, integrations, and adoption.
* Work with Technology and business leaders to improve service quality, operational readiness, system stability, and resiliency.
* Manage the service management budget and assigned resources, balancing service needs, risk, and cost.
* Set expectations for vendors and service providers supporting ITSM processes; monitor service levels, delivery, governance, and cost-effectiveness.
* Ensure service management policies and procedures reflect current practices and support compliance with applicable requirements, including SOX, PCI, IT audit, GDPR, and CCPA.
* Identify relevant technology and industry developments, including ITIL 4, ServiceNow, and DevOps practices, and assess their value to Hertz.
* Communicate service performance, risks, priorities, and improvement plans clearly to executives, business partners, employees, and vendors.
* Build effective working relationships across Technology and the business to coordinate service ownership and resolve operational issues.

**What We’re Looking For:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* ITIL 4 certification preferred;

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. The duty of this organization is to enable our Customers' ongoing Mission Readiness. From the moment they say "go" until the contract is fulfilled. We are only successful when the customer's mission is successful.

This team supports the Business Lines and Divisions throughout the lifecycle of their product, from initial sustainment concept through delivery, installation, operation, repair and return. These service offerings also include providing technical publications, training, customer support, connectivity services and other value-added services. To the degree the Business elects, we accept the delegated responsibility for upfront and continued delivery of the committed service solutions. This team endeavors to provide the Business Lines, as our internal customers, shared mission services that are more efficient and cost effective than if they chose to provide them directly. By offering mission support capabilities and capacity that are not "core" to the Business, the Business can focus resources on addressing the next big need while we ensure existing commitments are met.

You will create it. Where our Head of MRO is building and running the repair organization itself, this role owns the engineering rigor underneath it: the repair-versus-discard decisions, the maintenance task analyses, the repair procedures and the product support data that determine what gets fixed, how, and at what level. About ANELLO:

Founded by pioneers in silicon photonics and navigation sensor technology, ANELLO has developed integrated photonic system-on-chip technology for next generation navigation. ANELLO's SIPHOG™ optical gyroscope is based on its patented photonic integrated circuit technology. Our products are high performance, low-power, much smaller size and weight, at a fraction of the cost of traditional optical gyros used in industrial, aerospace and military applications. They enable reliable and accurate navigation and positioning across autonomous applications and within GPS-denied environments. ANELLO has a growing list of customers in commercial and defense segments and scaling production significantly due in part to contracts in the UAV/USV Defense segments.

The Role:

We are moving our gyroscope and IMU electronics from discrete boards to a single, highly integrated mixed signal ASIC. This chip is the step that takes optical-gyroscope precision into high-volume products. As Director, ASIC Engineering, you will own this chip from definition to production. You will lead the program through a top-tier ASIC design partner to first silicon in less than two years. Then you will build ANELLO's in house ASIC organization and define the chips that follow.

Why This Role:
- Full ownership. One chip, one leader. You make the key decisions, from partner selection to tapeout.
- A hard, interesting chip. Low-noise optical receivers, data converters, precision references, power stages, and an embedded processor that runs the IMU sensor hub, all on one die.
- Build from the ground up. Hire the first engineers, set the flows, and shape the in-house team for future generations.
- Real-world impact. Your silicon goes into navigation systems that people depend on when GPS fails.
- Executive visibility. The ASIC is central to the company roadmap, and you work directly with the leadership team.

What You Will Do:
- Own the ASIC program end to end: scope, schedule, budget, risk, and the tapeout decision.
- Lead vendor selection through RFI, RFP, and RFQ. Select the design partner, the process, and the foundry.
- Lead the design partner at the technical level. Drive the design reviews, and hold a high bar on verification and sign-off.
- Own the specification. Make sure that the ASIC is a drop-in replacement for today's discrete electronics.
- Integrate the work outside the partner's scope: signal-processing RTL, firmware, package, photonics, and test.
- Lead silicon bring-up, characterization, qualification, and the ramp to production.
- Hire a small, strong core team now, and grow it into ANELLO's in-house ASIC organization.

What You Bring:
- BS in Electrical Engineering or a related field. MS or PhD preferred.
- 15+ years in ASIC development, including 5+ years leading ASIC teams or programs.
- Hands-on roots in analog/mixed-signal design or verification. You have designed silicon yourself.
- A record of shipping mixed-signal ASICs from specification to volume

Under limited supervision, performs supervisory and administrative tasks in developing, implementing, and managing programs designed to effectively address district safety, security and operational needs. Employees are responsible for the supervision of the following district departments: Athletics, Facilities, School Nutrition, School Safety, Technology, and Transportation.
  
SALARY RANGE
  
The salary range for this role can be found in the provided link: Salary Scales
  
  
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
  
The following information is intended to describe the overall nature and scope of the work being performed in relation to the position. This is not a comprehensive listing of all the responsibilities or tasks; other work may be assigned when deemed appropriate:
  
  

* Provide leadership and support for the Athletics, Facilities, School Nutrition, School Safety, Technology, and Transportation Departments.
* Advise and serve as a resource to the Assistant Superintendent on all matters concerning the safety, security, and operations of the school district.
* Serve as the school district's liaison to related, external agencies and departments (ie police, homeland security, DYFS, etc.).
* Work directly with law enforcement agencies during critical incident situations and follow-up.
* Coordinate training and assistance to school and district-based administrators in matters of safety, security, and operations.
* Routinely and systematically evaluate the District Emergency Plans and adjust as needed.
* Assist/advise in the development of crisis management/emergency response plans as part of each school's safety plan.
* Ensure compliance with all codes and requirements related to safety, security, and operations.
* Monitors and updates of the State of Delaware Emergency Response Information Portal (ERIP)
* Lead district-wide implementation of the Standard Response Protocol (SRP), including staff and student training, drills, and consistent use of SRP language and procedures in all schools and district facilities.
* Monitor facilities operations to ensure that students have a safe, clean, attractive, pleasant, and smoothly functioning physical learning environment.
* Monitor school nutrition services to ensure students receive food of nutritious quality in an atmosphere of cleanliness and personal care.
* Monitor the district's transportation services to ensure the safe and timely transport of students.
* Monitor technology operations to ensure quality and secure infrastructure, hardware, and software are implemented and maintained in a customer service-oriented environment (to include a replacement cycle for old/broken hardware, the District 1:1 initiative in terms of hardware, etc.).
* Oversee all budgets and the budgeting process associated with the operational departments.
* Perform all other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

**U.S. Soccer Overview**

The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.

We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.

U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.

**Position Description**

The Director of Campus Security is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing all security operations at the Arthur M. Blank U.S. Soccer National Training Center. This role ensures the safety of athletes, staff, visitors, and assets while maintaining a secure and professional environment.

This position plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and security of the National Training Center, supporting the mission and values of the United States Soccer Federation.

**Primary Responsibilities**

*Security Operations & Risk Management*

* Develop and enforce comprehensive security policies, procedures, and protocols for the National Training Center.
* Oversee access control, surveillance systems, and perimeter security measures.
* Conduct security risk assessments and implement mitigation strategies.
* Lead emergency preparedness planning, including fire safety, severe weather response, and active threat protocols.
* Coordinate security for high-profile events, training camps, and international team visits.

*Personnel Management & Training*

* Supervise and manage on-site security personnel, including third-party security contractors.
* Develop and conduct regular security training programs for staff, athletes, and security personnel.
* Establish a security culture by promoting awareness and best practices throughout the campus.

*Incident Response & Investigations*

* Serve as the primary point of contact for security incidents, coordinating response efforts with local law enforcement, emergency services, and USSF leadership.
* Investigate security breaches, threats, and other incidents, ensuring timely reporting and resolution.
* Maintain detailed records of incidents and prepare reports for senior leadership.

*Collaboration & Compliance*

* Work closely with the Vice President of Security, and Director of Security Operations

This hands-on leader combines deep manufacturing process engineering with a disciplined continuous improvement approach to make production operations more consistent, efficient, safe, and cost-effective across Mom's Meals.

-401(k) match
-Life insurance
-Short-term disability
-Health, dental and vision insurance
-Maternity/paternity leave

The Director of Remote Technical Services owns ASD's remote engineering practice as a profit center, not a cost center. This leader builds, staffs and runs the team that remotely configures, commissions, programs and supports the security, AV and network systems ASD deploys nationwide: access control, video surveillance (VMS / NVR / cloud video), intrusion and alarm panels, AV and the underlying network. The role also leads the implementation and execution of ASD's monitoring programs.

* **Most of the install is commissioned remotely.** Configuration, programming, firmware, enrollment and turn-up shift from field techs and AASDIs to the remote bench and depot pre-staging, as a standard step in every project.

* **The business pulls the team in early.** Sales, PMO and Design scope and quote remote engineering at the front of the deal, not as a same-day scramble.
* **Outcomes are faster and better.** Fewer revisits, shorter time from install to turn-up, and clean handoff into managed security and recurring support.

About the Office of the City Administrator

The Office of the City Administrator and its 20+ divisions and departments operate core internal and public-facing essential services in to San Francisco residents and businesses. Our aim is to strengthen San Francisco by providing efficient and effective government services to increase safety and resiliency, support our local economy, and optimize capital planning and infrastructure all while prioritizing equity and inclusion.
The Office of the City Administrator’s Mission and Vision

Our vision is to lead the nation in public administration and to enable City departments to effectively deliver critical public services. We aim to help the city run better, to connect San Francisco residents and constituents to the vital public services they seek, and to create a meaningful and diverse work culture that is the place of choice for people who are invested in a career in public service.
We are committed to ensuring that the City services are inclusive, efficient, equitable, and culturally competent for San Franciscans of all races, ethnic backgrounds, religions, and sexual orientations. This commitment requires comprehensive review and thorough analysis of existing practices and policies to remove barriers to real inclusion. We are also committed to ensuring that we have a safe, equitable, and inclusive workplace for individuals of all races. This includes creating opportunities for hiring, promotion, training, and development, for all employees, including but not limited to, Black, Indigenous, and people of color (BIPOC).
To learn more about our departments, divisions, and programs, visit:  https://sf.gov/departments/city-administrator

Sierra Space Careers:
At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.

Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.

Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.

We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.

About the Role
Sierra Space is scaling from development programs into high-rate, repeatable production across a diversified portfolio of military and commercial systems, including satellites and spacecraft, propulsion systems, solar power systems, and the Dream Chaser spaceplane. As Director, Production Operations based in Madison, Wisconsin, you will play a critical role in executing the production strategy for propulsion development and manufacturing, building the operational systems required to deliver hardware at pace, at quality, and at cost.

This is an execution-focused leadership role for a proven operations professional with expertise in propulsion systems. Reporting to the Vice President, Production, you will lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines and additional enterprise products within Sierra Space's Madison facility. You will drive standardization of production processes, implement data-driven manufacturing systems, and build high-performing teams capable of scaling propulsion output while maintaining quality and efficiency. You will partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management to ensure production readiness and on-time delivery of critical propulsion systems for space and defense applications.
About You
Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.

We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

This Opportunity
WSP is seeking a Project Manager to manage projects for our Power Testing and Energization (PTE) group within the POWER Delivery Department. This position is posted in multiple Regional Office Locations with the ability to work remotely from a mutually acceptable location (please note in the application questions where you prefer to be located). The candidate selected for this position may work remotely full-time at a location other than a WSP designated office/job site. Employees may travel to a WSP office for periodic meetings.
Your Impact
We are looking for candidates with strong business acumen, business development experience (must be a Seller/Doer) and must have a solid background in electrical testing and commissioning. This is a very fast-paced job working on several short-term or long-term projects at a time that may last from a day to several weeks/months in duration.  This position will manage various types of testing projects including distribution, transmission and substation projects.
The successful candidate will be responsible for managing technical and financial aspects of PTE projects with responsibilities including, but not limited to:
•    Lead the project planning process including initiation, engineering involvement, construction coordination, testing and commissioning, and final project close out
•    Manage project implementation including project schedule, project budget and the project resources including external vendors and contractors
•    Serve as the primary project authority for assigned project personnel on major project-related issues
•    Direct project team and lead the project management process
•    Responsible for metrics tracking, associated reporting to stakeholders, and compliance with regulatory, corporate and department procedures during all the phases of the project
•    Taking a significant role in business development and preparing proposals
•    Developing scope of work criteria, budgets, schedules, and related project documents
•    Managing testing services on electric utility systems from 15kV to 765 kV class
•    Providing internal mentoring and leadership to junior team members
•    Leading project teams in a matrixed reporting environment
•    Organizing internal and external project status meetings
•    Interfacing with other POWER divisions as necessary (studies, substations, industrial, government, distribution, or construction)
•    This position will require travel, mostly regionally, with some national clients
•    Promote company culture and manage internal and external relationships
•    Manage status reporting, invoicing, accounts receivable and unbilled for each project
